narrative_summary: The S&P closed at 7,753.11, essentially flat, marking a fifth consecutive session capped beneath the unconfirmed 7,793.68 swing high — a record shelf that is now visibly distributing rather than extending. The bull skeleton is fully intact (50-day above a rising 200-day, price above every fib level, junk spreads at year-lows of 1.22, VIX 15.46 in the standard band) and Monte Carlo has firmed to its best adjusted up-skew of the arc at 65.77% up-first, but that still fails the 70% Late Bull threshold for a thirteenth straight session. Against that, participation keeps narrowing: net new 52-week highs at 1.08, McClellan only just off cycle lows, and 5-day MFI (~60) far below its Aug 4 peak of ~91 at a higher price. With extension at +9.89% above the 200-day, ERP pinned at 0.26% in the valuation-ceiling band and the ERP-confirmed floor 4.6% below spot, the posture stays trim-into-strength and patience — no add is justified until either the 7,793.68 high confirms with breadth expansion or price resets to the 7,610/7,554 fib band.

conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: When breadth and credit both diverge from price, elevate caution even if price has not yet broken down; headline strength with weak breadth indicates narrow leadership.

primary_tension: The strongest probability and credit backdrop of the entire arc (65.77% adjusted up-first, junk spreads at a year-low 1.22, VIX 15.46, price above every fib) is colliding with a five-session failure to extend beneath an unconfirmed 7,793.68 record high, decaying participation (net new 52-week highs at 1.08, McClellan only just off cycle lows), a multi-session money-flow divergence (5-day MFI ~60 versus ~91 on Aug 4 at a lower price), extension at +9.89% above the 200-day with Moderate exhaustion, and an ERP compressed to 0.26% inside the valuation-ceiling band — leaving the best bullish evidence set of the sequence still failing the 70% Late Bull threshold for a thirteenth consecutive session.
